record.paper_title: On a general Syracuse problem with conjectures
record.context_brief: Uniqueness and divergence for the (2^ν−1)n+1 family
record.original_question: For every integer ν≥3, define T(n)=n/2 when n is even and T(n)=((2^ν−1)n+1)/2 when n is odd. Is the only cycle Ω(1)=(1→2^{ν−1}→2^{ν−2}→…→2→1), so that C(2^ν−1,1)={Ω(1)}? Do the positive integers decompose as N=G(1)∪G(∞), with G(∞) nonempty?

evidence.quote: For the choice of the parameters a = 2 ν − 1 and b = 1 for ν ≥ 2. The corresponding map T is given by T (n) = { n/ 2 if n is even , ((2ν − 1)n + 1)/ 2 if n is odd .

Conjecture 5.7. Let ν ≥ 3 and let the parameters a = 2 ν − 1 and b = 1 , then the set C(a, b ) contains exactly one cycle, C(a, b ) = { Ω(1)} . We have N = G(1) ∪ G(∞ ), with G(∞ ) ̸= ∅ where the trivial cycle Ω(1), of length ν is Ω(1) = (1 → 2ν − 1 → 2ν − 2 → . . . → 2 → 1).
